market_summary: US markets are navigating significant leadership changes and legal challenges to major tech firms. Warren Buffett's stepping down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman ends an era, though the company has said succession planning has been in place. Meanwhile, Alphabet faces a $3.2 billion ad-tech damages lawsuit, and Microsoft is undergoing executive departures as the company reorganizes around AI priorities. Tesla stock remains under pressure, down about 20% year-to-date amid broader weakness in pure-play EV makers. Market attention has turned to personal AI agents as the next frontier, with investor focus shifting beyond language model capabilities.

items.headline: Warren Buffett Steps Down as Berkshire Hathaway Chairman
items.summary: <cite index="1-4,1-5,1-6">Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, effective immediately, and will become chairman emeritus while his son Howard replaces him as chairman. The legendary investor has led the company since 1965, posting a 19.7% compounded annual return.</cite>

items.headline: Alphabet Must Face $3.2 Billion Publisher Ad-Tech Damages Lawsuit, Judge Rules
items.summary: <cite index="21-6,21-7">A New York federal judge ruled that USA Today, Daily Mail and approximately 5,000 publishers can pursue over $3.2 billion in damages from Google, with claims centering on allegations that the company monopolized digital advertising technology markets.</cite>

items.headline: Google Unveils Gemini 4 Argon AI Model
items.summary: <cite index="10-3,10-4,10-5">Alphabet's Google announced a new flagship artificial intelligence model called Argon, which is larger than previous Pro models and described as comparable to frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic on coding and cybersecurity benchmarks.</cite>

items.headline: Ryan Roslansky, LinkedIn and Office Chief, to Exit Microsoft by End of 2026
items.summary: <cite index="42-1,42-3,42-4">Microsoft executive Ryan Roslansky, who led LinkedIn for six years and took on Office productivity responsibilities last year, will leave at the end of 2026, citing the need to be based in Redmond full-time while his life remains in the San Francisco Bay Area.</cite>

items.headline: Tesla Down 20% in 2026 as EV Market Faces Sharp De-Rating
items.summary: <cite index="29-8,29-9">Tesla stock is down 25% year to date, capturing the defining EV story of 2026: a sharp de-rating in the pure-play electric vehicle complex, even as legacy automakers and the broad tech tape have moved higher.</cite>
